description:
Why are people leaving India's villages? This investigative Hinglish documentary examines historical Census records and Uttarakhand migration research to understand the pressures behind village depopulation.

We distinguish permanent uninhabited status from seasonal migration, examine reported livelihood, education, health, infrastructure and agricultural pressures, and consider the strongest counter-argument: migration can also create opportunity. Historical figures are labelled with their source years and are not presented as current 2026 counts.

CHAPTERS
00:00 The Village That Went Silent
01:04 Title Card
01:13 A Country Built on Villages
02:32 The Himalayan Disappearance
03:49 The Economics of Leaving
05:26 When Essential Services Disappear
07:35 The Big Reveal: It Is Not One Cause
09:11 Can a Village Come Back?
11:24 The Door That Remains

RESEARCH SOURCES
- Government of India, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1156 (03 March 2016): https://sansad.in/getFile/loksabhaquestions/annex/7/AU1156.pdf
- Rural Development and Migration Commission, Interim Report on Status of Migration (April 2018): https://www.uttarakhandpalayanayog.com/pdf/Palayan%20Ayog%20Report_English.pdf
- MoSPI, Annual Report PLFS 2020-21: https://mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/publication_reports/Annual_Report_PLFS_2020%2021_0.pdf
- PIB release reporting PLFS migration indicators: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1833854&lang=2&reg=48
- PIB release reporting migration streams: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2042542&lang=2&reg=48

EDITORIAL NOTE
The 2011 Census and 2018 Uttarakhand survey figures are historical. Migration statistics are not counts of permanently abandoned villages. The Commission's 2018 report records revenue villages/toks/majra depopulated after 2011 and reports migration-reason and destination shares. Survey definitions and denominators should still be checked in the original tables before publication. AI-generated or reconstructed visuals are illustrative, not archival evidence.

AI DISCLOSURE

shorts_clips.hook_line: Census 2011 recorded 43,324 uninhabited villages in India—but what does that number really mean?
The leading reported reason for migration in the cited Uttarakhand data was lack of livelihood and employment.
A village doesn't disappear for one single reason. The causes can reinforce one another.
